children: By Wayne Cole

The Australian dollar broke to four-month highs on the greenback on Friday as markets pared the chance of a near-term rise in U.S. interest rates, while the New Zealand dollar struggled with a dovish shift in the policy outlook at home.
In contrast, data on economic growth and inflation have led investors to narrow the odds on the Reserve Bank of Australia hiking rates again when it meets later this month.
Markets now imply a 66% chance of a quarter-point rise to 4.60% this month, up from just 10% a couple of weeks ago. They also imply a 50% risk of a further move to 4.85%. (0#AUDIRPR)
The hawkish turn lifted the Aussie 0.2% to $0.7212
, having gained 0.4% overnight. The break of $0.72008 opens the way for a test of the 2026 high at $0.7277, while major support lies at $0.7122.
It had less luck on the Japanese yen, which rallied sharply as wagers on a Bank of Japan rate hike helped squeeze crowded short positions. That saw the Aussie recoil to 112.17 yen
, well off the recent 36-year peak of 114.98.
The kiwi dollar found some support at $0.5890
, after bouncing 0.5% overnight and away from a trough of $0.5802. It was still down 0.6% for the week and needs to get back above $0.5928 to stabilise the technical outlook.

The currency was hit hard on Wednesday when the Reserve Bank of New Zealand lifted interest rates a quarter point to 2.75% as expected, but projected a much more gradual and limited tightening path than markets had looked for.

Investors have sharply scaled back expectations for another hike in October, but are still pricing a move to 3.0% in December. Swaps also imply an eventual top of 3.5%, when the RBNZ had projected a peak of 3.15%. (0#NZDIRPR)
The shift in rate risks saw the kiwi shed 1% for the week on the Aussie, which touched a 13-year peak of NZ$1.2285
at one stage.
"Those technically inclined will also note that the next major high is at NZ$1.3796, recorded in March 2011," said Rodrigo Catril, a senior FX strategist at NAB.
"AUD/NZD has the potential to break above NZ$1.23, and a stretch up to as high as NZ$1.25, only about 2% away, certainly can't be ruled out."
He was more bearish on the Aussie for next year, seeing a retreat to NZ$1.1100 as the RBA was more likely to start easing in late 2027, ahead of the RBNZ.
